Specifically, it uses `curl` to fetch data from `api.github.com` without any checks or sanitization, and relies on fragile text parsing (grep/sed) of JSON responses. 1. The `curl` command runs unconditionally during sourcing of the PKGBUILD, meaning that simply running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will trigger an external HTTP request.

3. Although the fetched data is intended for versioning, executing network calls and processing remote content during PKGBUILD parse time creates a supply-chain risk — an attacker compromising the API response could potentially influence build behavior.

Even though no code execution from the downloaded files occurs at this stage due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, the act of automatically contacting an external service and parsing its response during PKGBUILD sourcing violates security best practices for offline reproducibility and introduces a covert channel.

This is especially concerning because `_update_version` runs before any user-controlled guard (like `_srcinfo` or `_pkgver`) can skip it — the condition `[ "${_autoupdate::1}" != "t" ]` defaults to true unless explicitly disabled, and the function runs immediately upon sourcing.
